note: The proverbs' shelf (mathal-*): every contradiction tools/grammar_audit.js listed on the new packages (35 on the first full run) judged by the line. Two were the author's and were corrected in the scripts (listed under «corrected»): يَعْجِزُ (the head-sentence note moved to the mubtadaʾ) and قُرَاقِر (the diptote's fatha named); حَيَّاكَ and وَتَمْرًا had the maqūl seat added to the line, and the engine still reads another seat first (judged E). Second full run: 33 on the shelf, all judged. The rest: E = the engine is wrong by the books, C = both readings are allowed.

records.why: the author reads «يَغْصِبُهُمْ» as a second predicate of كَانَ after «عَنِيفًا»; the engine offers a ḥāl of «مَمْلَكَتِهِ» or a fresh start. A kāna may take more than one khabar (al-Inṣāf's own gloss: «ومصيف: خبر ثان»), so both readings stand.

cite.ar: فَبَتِّي: خبر المبتدأ الذي هو هذا، ومصيف: خبر ثان، ومقيظ: خبر ثالث

records.why: «عِنْدَ الصَّبَاحِ» is a ẓarf and «يَحْمَدُ» the main verb of the proverb; there is no noun for a ḥāl or naʿt clause to describe.
the author's line already says «مُعْتَرِضَةٌ لَا مَحَلَّ لَهَا» — the engine reads the line's earlier «خَبَرِيَّةٌ لَفْظًا» as a khabar seat.
«انْظُرُوا» opens what Rāfiʿ says after «قَالَ رَافِعٌ:» — the maqūl, not a naʿt or khabar of the speaker's name.
«أَنَّى» is the question noun «how» in the seat of a ḥāl (wonder); it is no mubtadaʾ or nāsikh to own «اهْتَدَى» as its khabar.
there is no condition in the rajaz line: «فَوَّزَ» opens a new clause after «أَنَّى اهْتَدَى».
«الرَّجُلُ» is the doer of «فَقَالَ»; «أَطْعِمْنِي» opens what he says (maqūl), not his khabar.
«ضَبَّةُ» is the doer of «فَقَالَ»; «أَرِنِي» opens what he says (maqūl), not his khabar.
after «قَوْلًا رَابِعًا:» the colon introduces what the account says; «زَعَمَ …» spells the account out (tafsīr), it does not qualify «رَابِعًا».
«أَحَيًّا» is the hamza and a fronted ḥāl; «تَرَى» is the verb of the question, not a naʿt or khabar of «حَيًّا».
the token is «بِ» + the dual «خُفَّيْ»: the line's sign (the ya of the dual) belongs to the noun; the engine reads the jarr letter's built state.
the rhyme word stands in pause with its tāʾ said and written as hāʾ («الْجَهَالَهْ»): the case sign is estimated, hidden by the pause — the engine wants a written vowel the verse cannot carry.
the rhyme word stands in pause («الْمَحَالَهْ»): the raf' is estimated, hidden by the pause.
the rhyme word stands in pause («الْمَقَالَهْ»): the raf' is estimated, hidden by the pause.
«أَصْوَاتَ» is a broken plural (أَفْعَال of صَوْت), its tāʾ a root letter: in nasb by the fatha, not the kasra of the sound feminine plural.
the lam of «لَأَرْغَبُ» is the lām of emphasis moved to the predicate of «إِنِّي», not the lām of command; the verb stays in raf'.
«فَنُضَيِّعَ» follows the fa of consequence answering the negation «وَلَمْ تَحْمِلْنَا»: in nasb by an implied أَنْ, not jazm.
«وَنَبْخَسَكَ» is conjoined to «فَنُضَيِّعَ» and shares its nasb.
«بِخُفَّيْ حُنَيْنٍ»: the dual in jarr with its nun dropped for the annexation; no helping kasra is due before a name without the article.
«فَيَلْبَسَ» follows the fa of consequence answering the negation «لَمْ يُقْبَلْ»: in nasb by an implied أَنْ, not jazm.
«تَرَوْنَ» is one of the five verbs in raf' by the kept nun after «هَلْ»; nothing puts it in jazm.
«فَلَمْ يُوَلِّهِ» is Form II «وَلَّى يُوَلِّي» in jazm by the dropped ya, active (the caliph is its doer), not the passive «يُوَلَّهُ».
«بَيْنَمَا» is the ẓarf بَيْنَ with the restraining مَا, built on its fatha; it is no predicate of إِنَّ and wears no tanwin.
«فَبَيْنَمَا» is the ẓarf بَيْنَ with the restraining مَا; it is no mubtadaʾ and wears no tanwin.
«لِئَلَّا تَرْعَى» gives the purpose of muzzling: it hangs on «كَعَمَ», not on the noun «أَفْوَاهَهَا».
«وَبَيْنَ يَدَيْ عَمْرٍو» is a fronted predicate in a ḥāl clause («وَبَيْنَ يَدَيْ عَمْرٍو زُبْدٌ»); it does not hang on «الْعَطَشُ».
«كُلَّمَا» is a ẓarf that hangs on its answer «قَالَ»; the whole كُلَّمَا clause is the khabar of كَانَ, the ẓarf itself does not hang on an omitted khabar.
«وَمَعَهُ الْحَارِثُ» is a ḥāl clause whose fronted khabar «مَعَهُ» hangs on an omitted «كائن» (mustaqarr), not on «يَسِيرُ».
«قَدْ تَرَى مَا نَحْنُ فِيهِ»: «مَا» is the relative «what (we are in)», the object of «تَرَى»; it is no negating مَا that suspends a heart verb.
«وَأَنَّ ابْنَ عَمِّهِ أَرَادَ سَدَّهُ» is conjoined to «أَنَّ ابْنَ عَمٍّ …» inside «وَكَانَ مِنْ خَبَرِ هٰذَا الشِّعْرِ أَنَّ …»: it keeps the fatha.
«وَإِنَّ امْرَأَةً لَهُ سَمِعَتْ» opens a new sentence after a full stop: the hamza takes kasra; nothing governs it to be conjoined in the fatha.
the line now states the maqūl seat («فِي مَحَلِّ نَصْبٍ مَقُولُ الْقَوْلِ»); the engine reads the earlier «خَبَرِيَّةٌ لَفْظًا» (a statement in form, a prayer in meaning) as a khabar seat.

the line states both: the clause «وَتَمْرًا» (with its implied verb) is conjoined to «كِلَاهُمَا», and «كِلَاهُمَا وَتَمْرًا» together are what is said; the engine takes the conjunction as the clause's only seat.
